scope: Navigation startup quality preference; no public-reference tuning

failure_names: RTK arriving after low-quality fixes owns the anchor
absent RTK falls back at the unchanged five-second deadline
one RTK fix cannot promote a lower-quality window early
low-quality rover cannot rotate an RTK master anchor
coherent RTK pair survives denser low-quality timestamps
RTK rover fallback is not blocked by low-quality master
reset restarts quality evidence and deadline
moving startup prefers RTK without losing wheel travel

test_names: RTK arriving after low-quality fixes owns the anchor
absent RTK falls back at the unchanged five-second deadline
one RTK fix cannot promote a lower-quality window early
sparse RTK remains usable at the deadline without mixing qualities
low-quality rover cannot rotate an RTK master anchor
coherent RTK pair survives denser low-quality timestamps
RTK rover fallback is not blocked by low-quality master
RTK rover respects its delay with either antenna arrival order
stale RTK pair cannot provide startup heading
reset restarts quality evidence and deadline
reset discards unfinished RTK and lower-quality fallback windows
moving startup prefers RTK without losing wheel travel
stale and future RTK cannot satisfy startup evidence
no GNSS still releases relative position after five seconds

policy: Keep status=2 samples and timestamps separate from lower-quality samples per antenna.
Before deadline, master RTK requires startup_min_fixes; rover RTK requires minimum count, no RTK master yet, and existing rover delay.
At deadline select sufficient master RTK, sufficient rover RTK, sparse master RTK, sparse rover RTK, usable master, then usable rover.
Sparse RTK may anchor only at deadline; never mix quality groups in position median or heading pair.
Retain existing timestamp age, pairing time/baseline/coherence, moving-distance and reset rules.
coverage_expectation: Runs beginning with status0/1 hold position until RTK minimum count or first event after five seconds; velocity publication continues. RTK-first and no-GNSS deadlines unchanged. Public coverage and trajectory effects are for frozen-code evaluation, not tuning.
limitations: Early RTK rover waits if any RTK master sample exists, preserving master preference until deadline.
Quality preference affects startup only; ongoing correction policy is unchanged.
